## Left open by the earlier read (RD-110)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule B01 (Blocker). Problem: This treats all pre-1973 births as reaching majority at 21. Someone born in 1972 reached 18 after RA 6809 lowered majority in 1989. The applicable majority age depends on when adulthood was reached, not simply on being born before 1973. The supplied brief does not support this blanket historical instruction.
   > The majority age for the older citizenship-election cases was $21$. Republic Act $6809$ later lowered the general majority age to $18$. Do not use today's age to decide when someone born before $1973$ reached adulthood.
2. Rule L08 (Major). Problem: This lesson is designated Filipino, but its teaching prose is in English. It does not teach in simple Filipino at the Grade 5 standard.
   > Citizenship** means legal membership in a country. Many public offices and rights depend on it.
3. Rule L10 (Major). Problem: This lesson is designated Filipino, but all 11 worked examples use English questions and solutions. The examples must be in Filipino.
   > A child born in $2005$ has a Filipino mother and an alien father. Is the child a Philippine citizen from birth?
4. Rule L12 (Minor). Problem: This lesson is designated Filipino, but its teaching prose uses full English sentences throughout. These are not isolated common English terms in Filipino prose.
   > An **alien** is a citizen of another country. To **elect citizenship** means to formally choose it as the law requires.
5. Rule L27 (Major). Problem: The historical-election condition is misstated as a single age rule for everyone born before 1973. It must distinguish people who reached adulthood before and after RA 6809 changed the majority age. Otherwise students are told to apply the wrong age to part of the covered group.
   > The majority age for the older citizenship-election cases was $21$. Republic Act $6809$ later lowered the general majority age to $18$. Do not use today's age to decide when someone born before $1973$ reached adulthood.

### Accuracy concerns

1. This treats all pre-1973 births as reaching majority at 21. Someone born in 1972 reached 18 after RA 6809 lowered majority in 1989. The applicable majority age depends on when adulthood was reached, not simply on being born before 1973. The supplied brief does not support this blanket historical instruction.
   > The majority age for the older citizenship-election cases was $21$. Republic Act $6809$ later lowered the general majority age to $18$. Do not use today's age to decide when someone born before $1973$ reached adulthood.

## Left open by the earlier read (RD-110)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L25 (Major). Problem: CPA is needed to use the COA eligibility rule but is never expanded or explained. COMELEC and COA are also introduced without their full institutional names. No supplied prerequisite teaches these meanings.
   > They must be CPAs with at least $10$ years of auditing experience or lawyers with at least $10$ years of practice.
